raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #44770. Split per review: this PR keeps the adapter-state and merge-transition fixes. Format/scaling and merge-cache changes moved to separate PRs.

## Changes

- Clear existing adapters on the first adapter that covers a layer (not index 0), so adapters no longer stack when adapter 0 misses a layer.
- `set_lora` skips only when every target module already matches.
- Critic offload lookups map `critic` to `fake_score_transformer`.
- `load_lora_adapter` builds into a local dict and swaps at the end, so a failed reload keeps the previous adapter.
- Dynamic reactivation fast path only requires covered layers to hold exactly one entry.
- An explicit `merge_lora_weights(strength=...)` is compared against every adapter's strength and updates `cur_adapter_config`.

## Tests

No new files; extended `test_lora_pipeline.py` and `test_fused_lora_compose.py`. The new tests fail on `main` and pass here.

Modal CPU, targeted LoRA unit files: pass. ruff, isort, codespell clean. No GPU run.

nodes.body: Hi @mickqian, please review this pr. Thank you!
Hi @BBuf, please provide an initial review of this PR when you have time. Thank you!

Please reduce both the implementation diff and test code to the minimum needed for the fixes. When splitting the adapter-state, format/scaling, and cache changes, keep each fix and its focused regression together; leave broader refactors for follow-ups.

The tests should reuse existing LoRA fixtures and parameterize equivalent cases instead of repeating pipeline construction and mocks. Keep a small set of meaningful weight/output comparisons for adapter switching, strength overrides, alpha scaling, and cache reuse. Please consolidate overlapping coverage and avoid adding tests that only mirror internal bookkeeping when an existing behavioral test can catch the same bug.

Re https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44309#discussion_r4333930256 (group adapter metadata into one record): this touches about 40 references across pipeline.py and five test files, and the PRs split out of #44309 each use different dicts. Since it is non-blocking, would you be fine leaving it out here and doing it in a separate scoped PR once these land?

This still combines three independently reviewable areas: adapter state/merge transitions, format and alpha/rank conversion, and persistent merge-cache identity/eviction. Please split along those boundaries, keeping each regression with its fix; one PR per individual bug is unnecessary.

Two concrete issues remain: an explicit strength override can be skipped when only the first adapter's strength matches, and the cache key does not include the effective per-adapter alpha/configuration. I reproduced both decisions with small CPU inputs. The other inline comments are non-blocking cleanup/test suggestions; no real-model/offload/DTensor GPU validation was performed.

Please also refresh the description for the final implementation: public merge APIs still default to 1.0 (None is explicit), and `_convert_with_diffusers_utils_if_available` is still present.

[P2] An explicit override still gets skipped for mixed adapter strengths. `set_lora` records only `tgt_strengths[0]` in `cur_adapter_strength`, so an already-merged `[0.5, 1.0]` configuration followed by `merge_lora_weights(strength=0.5)` takes this early return and leaves the second adapter at 1.0. I reproduced zero layer-merge calls and the unchanged `[0.5, 1.0]` config. Could we compare the requested strength against every active adapter's strength, and extend the existing override regression to this case?

nodes.body: Non-blocking cache-policy follow-up: could eviction participate in admission before writing a new store, rather than only run after successful `finalize()`? If existing stores consume the available disk headroom, `_ensure_writable()` returns false, no entries are written, and `finalize()` returns before reaching this eviction. The cache then keeps the old stores and cannot reclaim them to admit the next combination. A deterministic low-space test can cover the desired reclaim-versus-fallback behavior.

inline_comments.body: Non-blocking cache-policy follow-up: could eviction participate in admission before writing a new store, rather than only run after successful `finalize()`? If existing stores consume the available disk headroom, `_ensure_writable()` returns false, no entries are written, and `finalize()` returns before reaching this eviction. The cache then keeps the old stores and cannot reclaim them to admit the next combination. A deterministic low-space test can cover the desired reclaim-versus-fallback behavior.

issue_comments.body: Hi @mickqian, please review this pr. Thank you!
Hi @BBuf, please provide an initial review of this PR when you have time. Thank you!

Please reduce both the implementation diff and test code to the minimum needed for the fixes. When splitting the adapter-state, format/scaling, and cache changes, keep each fix and its focused regression together; leave broader refactors for follow-ups.

The tests should reuse existing LoRA fixtures and parameterize equivalent cases instead of repeating pipeline construction and mocks. Keep a small set of meaningful weight/output comparisons for adapter switching, strength overrides, alpha scaling, and cache reuse. Please consolidate overlapping coverage and avoid adding tests that only mirror internal bookkeeping when an existing behavioral test can catch the same bug.

Re https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44309#discussion_r4333930256 (group adapter metadata into one record): this touches about 40 references across pipeline.py and five test files, and the PRs split out of #44309 each use different dicts. Since it is non-blocking, would you be fine leaving it out here and doing it in a separate scoped PR once these land?

reviews.body:
This still combines three independently reviewable areas: adapter state/merge transitions, format and alpha/rank conversion, and persistent merge-cache identity/eviction. Please split along those boundaries, keeping each regression with its fix; one PR per individual bug is unnecessary.

Two concrete issues remain: an explicit strength override can be skipped when only the first adapter's strength matches, and the cache key does not include the effective per-adapter alpha/configuration. I reproduced both decisions with small CPU inputs. The other inline comments are non-blocking cleanup/test suggestions; no real-model/offload/DTensor GPU validation was performed.

Please also refresh the description for the final implementation: public merge APIs still default to 1.0 (None is explicit), and `_convert_with_diffusers_utils_if_available` is still present.
